names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 26 Μαΐου, «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος από την Θεσσαλονίκη ο Δερβίσης», with the rank word left off and the by-name kept, as the page's own head line prints it.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 26. мај ст. ст., „Свети новомученик Александар Солунски“ — Свети is not a rank and новомученик is the `new-martyr` this corpus puts in `types`; strip the two and „Александар Солунски“ is left. **Солунски is kept because it is what tells him from the corpus’s other Alexanders and because the heading prints it as part of the name**, and it was measured: `foldchk.py` returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Александар Солунски», where a bare «Александар» would have folded onto a long column for nothing. **Дервиш is not in the stored form** although the display name keeps it: this heading does not print it, and a form is copied and not composed. The Greek form on this folder, «Αλέξανδρος», is the bare one.

death.note: saint.gr: «υπέμεινε με καρτερία το μαρτυρικό του θάνατο δι' αποκεφαλισμού, στις 26 Μαΐου 1794», and the head line «(; - 1794)».

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 26ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος από την Θεσσαλονίκη ο Δερβίσης»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 26 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», and the page puts his beheading on that same 26 May of 1794, so the feast is the day of the death. None of the corpus's men of this name is a Thessalonian who apostatised at Smyrna, entered the order of the dervishes and came back. Two hymns are copied, both proper to him and naming Thessalonica; the megalynarion the page also prints cannot be held by the schema's `kind` enum. The page names Laodigia or Lagodiani, «σημερινή Λαοδηγήτρια», as his quarter, and no `locations` object is proposed for a quarter of a city.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 08.06.2026 (26. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети новомученик Александар Солунски“

attestations.note: The day’s fourth entry, on the same menologion 26/5 the Greek row already carries. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of the 23 to 26 May is. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND CORROBORATED TO THE DAY AND THE PLACE.** The folder holds `death` 1794 off saint.gr’s „on 26 May 1794“. The Prologue says „Би посечен у Смирни 1794. године“ — beheaded at Smyrna in 1794 — so the year, the manner and the city are all confirmed by a second book, and there is nothing to widen and nothing to narrow. **„у време велике тираније турске над овим градом“ is a period and not a year**, and no date is taken from it. **THE TWO BOOKS TELL THE APOSTASY DIFFERENTLY, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE REASON FOR IT.** saint.gr has him come young to Smyrna **fleeing the lewd designs of a Turk**, and says that there, **„for reasons unknown to us“ — the page’s own words — he renounced his faith**. **The Prologue gives a reason**: „Као младић заваран би од Турака и потурчен“ — as a youth he was deceived by the Turks and made a Turk — **and it puts the apostasy at no city at all**, where saint.gr puts it at Smyrna. **A reason stated against a reason refused is not a contradiction and neither account was altered**: both stand in the life, and the Greek page’s own confession of ignorance is left standing beside this book’s answer. **AND THE REPENTANCE BEGINS IN A DIFFERENT PLACE IN EACH.** This book has him come to **the Kaaba with the other Muhammadan pilgrims**, become a dervish, and then **as a dervish in Thessalonica begin bitterly to repent**; saint.gr has him visit Mecca, enter the order, feign madness and wander the subject countries **eighteen years**, rebuke the Turkish tyranny, keep Great Lent in a Christian church on **Chios** in his dervish’s clothes, and only then come to Smyrna and strip the clothes off before the judge. **The eighteen years, Chios and the trampling are saint.gr’s alone; the Kaaba, Thessalonica and the reasoning are this book’s.** **New here, and the heart of it is one argument and one sentence**: that in his repentance **he came to the thought that he could wash the dreadful sin of apostasy from himself by nothing but his own blood**, and so resolved on martyrdom and declared himself a Christian before the Turks; that under torture he only cried **„Као хришћанин сам рођен, као хришћанин хоћу да умрем“** — as a Christian I was born, as a Christian I will die; and that when they condemned him **he rejoiced greatly, knowing from it that his sins were forgiven and that God accepted his sacrifice**. **He was also born at Thessalonica**, which the display name already says and which saint.gr gives only as where he came from. `new-martyr` is corroborated outright and **no type was added**: Дервиш is not a rank in this corpus’s vocabulary and the epithet is already in the display name. `related` stays empty, the entry naming nobody with a folder. No `locations`, although Thessalonica, the Kaaba and Smyrna are all named. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the two Greek hymns on this folder stay.

hymns.text: Ἐν ἀθλήσει νομίμως Μάρτυς ἠρίστευσας, καὶ τὸν σὲ τρώσαντα πρῲην κατηγωνίσω ἐχθρὸν, καὶ Μαρτύρων κοινωνὸς ὤφθης Ἀλέξανδρε. Ὅθεν ὡς ἅγιον βλαστόν, Θεσσαλονίκη σὲ τιμᾷ, καὶ πόθῳ σοι ἀνακράζει· Μὴ διαλίπῃς πρεσβεύων, ἐλεηθῆναι τοὺς τιμῶντάς σε.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἦχος πλ. α’, Τὸν συνάναρχον Λόγον, on the page of «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος από την Θεσσαλονίκη ο Δερβίσης»

english.text: You contended lawfully and excelled in the contest, O martyr, and overcame the enemy who had wounded you before, and were shown a companion of the martyrs, Alexander. Therefore Thessalonica honours you as a holy shoot and cries out to you with longing: do not cease from interceding, that mercy may be shown to those who honour you.

hymns.text: Ἑορτάζει σήμερον, Θεσσαλονίκη ἡ πόλις, τὴν ἁγίαν μνήμην σου, Ἀλέξανδρε Νεομάρτυς· ταύτης γὰρ, γόνος καὶ βλάστημα θεῖον πέλων, ἤθλησας, ἐν Σμύρνῃ γνώμῃ ἀνδρειοτάτῃ, δι’ ἀγάπην τοῦ Κυρίου· ὅν ἐκδυσώπει σώζεσθαο ἅπαντας.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἦχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον, on the page of «Άγιος Αλέξανδρος από την Θεσσαλονίκη ο Δερβίσης»

english.text: Today the city of Thessalonica keeps your holy memory, Alexander the new martyr; for being her offspring and her divine shoot, you contended at Smyrna with a most manly resolve, for the love of the Lord. Entreat him that all may be saved.
